title: The Burning Hollow Revisited
premise: Noor Halloran, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that fell silent a decade ago, keeps the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things—stolen years, borrowed names, unmade debts. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin answering themselves across the city of Vell, Noor discovers their silent god is not dead but imprisoned, its voice stolen by the thing wearing King Aldric's crown. To free it, Noor must ally with Sefa, a disgraced royal inquisitor hunting the same truth from the other side of the law, and descend into the Burning Hollow beneath the palace where the first gods were bound. In the end, Noor breaks their own oath to shatter the crown's binding, freeing the god at the cost of their guild's protection—and chooses love and an unwritten future over the survival they were sworn to preserve.
about_author: Yara Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing medieval debt records before turning to fantasy. They write about ledgers, oaths, and the people trapped between them from a drafty house on the northern coast.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Noor auditing the Hollow Guild's strangest accounts—a jar of borrowed laughter, a widow's purchased grief—while quietly mourning their silent god. A routine entry for 'one king's shadow' arrives with no buyer listed. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the first wrong note.

chapters.title: Prayers That Answer Back
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Across Vell, shrines begin glowing; a beggar's prayer cures his fever instantly. The Guild panics—answered prayers mean old gods awake, and awake gods collect on ancient debts. Noor tests their own silent god with a prayer and receives, for the first time in ten years, silence that feels like listening.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Royal inquisitor Sefa interrogates a priest driven mad by answered prayers and finds the same phrase carved into his skin: THE CROWN REMEMBERS. Ordered to suppress all evidence, she instead copies it. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt as she realizes her orders protect something, not someone.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The Guildmaster reveals the 'king's shadow' entry is decades old—an unpaid price from the Binding of Aldric, when the Guild helped put something on the throne to end a war. Noor realizes their god went silent the same year. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ledger they trusted was complicit.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sefa raids the Guild seeking the shadow-ledger; Noor catches her mid-theft. Instead of fighting, they trade information over stolen wine—her carved priests, his ledger entries. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who both serve broken institutions.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa gains audience with King Aldric and watches him pause mid-sentence, eyes going flat and golden, before resuming perfectly. She confirms the king is a puppet maintained by something older. Emotional beat: horror wrapped in courtly composure; she can no longer pretend not to know.

chapters.title: The God That Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following a decade-old map in their own oath-mark, Noor finds a hidden shrine where their god left one final message before falling silent: a name—Vessarine—and a warning: do not let it finish counting. Emotional beat: grief transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: Guild Justice
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The Guildmaster, fearing exposure, orders Noor's memory purchased and erased—the Guild's own impossible trade turned against them. Noor escapes with the ledger and burns their bridge behind them. Emotional beat: exile; the price of survival is belonging.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Noor and Sefa shelter in the Undercroft, a haven for the legally dead. Among smugglers and erased citizens, Noor sees what justice looks like when no law will carry it. Emotional beat: tenderness growing between them amid shared fugitive exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Counting Begins
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Across Vell, people who made bargains with the crown begin dying at dawn, their lives collected as interest. Sefa maps the deaths and finds they form a countdown—fourteen days. Emotional beat: dread with a deadline; the abstract threat acquires teeth.

chapters.title: A Bargain with the Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. To reach the Hollow, Noor needs passage through the river-gate, guarded by the Drowned Choir—drowned petitioners of the old gods. They demand a voice in payment. Noor offers their god's name instead, gambling everything on faith. Emotional beat: desperate devotion rewarded with uneasy passage.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa confronts her mentor, Lord Chancellor Ives, who confesses he helped bind Aldric to save the city from a worse war—and believes the crown's harvest is a fair price. He offers her promotion and silence. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of acceptable evil; she refuses.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Ash Market
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ives sends crown-guarded hunters after them both. A chase through the ash market ends with Sefa wounded shielding Noor. Hiding in a burned chapel, Noor prays aloud and the chapel answers—warmth, light, their god straining toward them. Emotional beat: love confessed under threat of death.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With nine days left, the pair decode the ledger: the Binding requires a willing oath-bearer to undo it, which is why the crown has been hunting oath-sworn survivors like Noor. The harvest isn't random—it's searching for the key. Emotional beat: the trap revealed; Noor is both lock and key.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Price
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The captured Guildmaster offers the crown Noor's location in exchange for the Guild's survival—but secretly slips Noor the original Binding contract, choosing redemption over safety. Emotional beat: an antagonist's grace note; even the compromised can choose once.

chapters.title: Descent into the Burning Hollow
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor and Sefa enter the Hollow beneath the palace, a cavern where the first gods were chained, lit by veins of slow fire. They find Noor's god, Vessarine, half-consumed, still whispering counter-prayers against the crown. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak—meeting the divine as a prisoner.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the King
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crown-entity manifests, offering each of them their deepest want: Sefa's reinstatement and honor, Noor's god restored whole if they walk away. It shows them Aldric, alive inside, begging for release. Emotional beat: temptation rendered intimate; refusal costs visible pieces of themselves.

chapters.title: An Oath Unbound
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the Hollow's heart, Noor understands: the binding feeds on oaths, so only a broken oath can break it. Speaking the renunciation they've dreaded for ten years, Noor unbinds themselves from Vessarine—and uses the severed oath as the blade. Emotional beat: sacrifice as climax; freedom chosen over protection.

chapters.title: The Counting Ends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The crown cracks; the entity unravels screaming as freed gods surge through Vell, collecting nothing, forgiving debts. Aldric dies human and grateful in Sefa's arms. Ives is arrested by his own guards. Emotional beat: catharsis—the harvest stops, the city breathes.

chapters.title: What Survives the Fire
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the aftermath, Noor is mortal, unprotected, and finally present. Vessarine, freed but diminished, offers to restore their oath. Noor declines—some prices shouldn't be paid twice. Emotional beat: quiet grief for the god, and peace with the choice.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa testifies before the provisional council, refusing to soften the Guild's crimes or her own complicity, and argues for justice that includes the erased. She and Noor open a small office: debts forgiven, names returned, oaths arbitrated. Emotional beat: justice rebuilt outside the law that failed.

chapters.title: The Burning Hollow, Revisited
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. One year later, Noor returns to the sealed Hollow and leaves a single entry in a new ledger: paid in full. Above ground, Sefa waits with breakfast and no agenda. The gods answer prayers now, gently. Emotional beat: earned rest; love without duty's shadow, and a life finally unwritten.
